item.title: NY State Senate GOP want New York's taxpayers to 'keep what they've earned'
item.description: New York Republican State Senators have proposed a legislative package to cut income and property taxes, limit government spending, and provide tax relief for families and businesses.

item.title: NY bill lets religious groups bypass zoning for housing on holy land
item.description: Faith leaders and Democratic lawmakers in New York are pushing for the Faith-Based Affordable Housing Act, which would allow religious organizations to build affordable housing on their property, bypassing local zoning restrictions and potentially creating 60,000 new homes statewide over the next decade.

item.title: Eyewitness Sports Scoreboard for Thursday, January 5
item.description: The Section III Girls' Volleyball Sectionals kicked off on Wednesday, and several teams took another step toward Central Valley Academy and the championship matches! We also had lots of action on the basketball court as they head toward the last weeks of their regular season, and you can catch up with everything on the Thursday edition of the Eyewitness Sports Scoreboard!

item.title: Salisbury man arrested on child sexual abuse charges
item.description: A Salisbury man is now in custody after New York State Police allege that he engaged in sexual conduct with a child.

item.title: CNY animal shelter announces fresh slate of board members after former leadership stepped down
item.description: DEWITT, N.Y. item.title: Assembly Minority Leader Will Barclay resigning after 23 years representing CNY
item.description: Assembly Minority Leader Will Barclay announced he will not seek reelection and plans to resign his leadership post in the coming days, leaving after 23 years in the state Assembly and five years leading the Republican Assemblymembers.

item.title: Albany rally seeks $62.1 million more for supportive housing
item.description: Housing advocates and lawmakers rallied at the New York State Capitol to demand more funding for supportive housing programs, which provide shelter for people living on the street, and save lives and money.

item.title: New York increasing violation points to curb dangerous driving
item.description: ALBANY, N.Y. (NEWS10) -- Some traffic violations in the state of New York will have increased point values beginning on Monday, Feb. 16. In addition to the updated points, the lookback timeframe for the Department of Motor Vehicles to take administrative action against a persistent violator increases from 18 months to 24 months.
